lines.text: ...You came down. Most never find the door.

lines: I am Fern. I keep the roots from wandering off. Mostly, I fail.

lines.text: There is a tree here that gives everything back. Pick up a leaf. You will see.

choices.text: Why can't you leave it alone?
I will look at the tree.

lines.text: You have been here before. The tree remembers you even if you do not.

lines: I keep the roots from wandering. You keep coming back to them.

lines.text: Pick up a leaf. It will be back before you finish turning around.

choices.text: Why can't you leave it alone?
I will look at the tree.

lines: Because it is mine to keep, and keeping is not the same as carrying.

lines.text: Go on. Take the leaf. Learn what it wants.
Good. I will be here. I am always here.
You understand it now. The leaf does not want to be carried.

lines: It wants only to be left where it falls, again and again, until someone lets it.
You could leave through the roots. Or you could let it stay.

lines.text: You know this tree already. You knew it in some other turning of the world.

lines: It does not hold that against you. It only asks the same thing again.
Leave it through the roots, or let it stay.

lines.text: The leaf settles. The roots stop reaching.

lines: Thank you. It will be quiet for a while now.

lines.text: The roots settle as if they had been waiting for you specifically.

lines: Some knots only come loose when someone remembers they were ever tied.

lines.text: Take your time. The tree certainly will.
The leaf has not come back. That is the first quiet I have had in a long while.

lines: Whatever you did, keep it. I will.
